name: Displacing Signals Detachment
location_context: Forward signals detachment, temperate northern Europe, early spring. No host-nation supply. The detachment is under orders to be able to displace at one hour's notice. SYNTHETIC scenario, not a real location.

grid_availability.note: SYNTHETIC. No host-nation supply is available at this location at any point in the mission.

weather_profile.description: Temperate northern Europe, early spring, mostly overcast (SYNTHETIC)

mobility_requirement.note: The detachment must be able to displace at one hour's notice for the whole mission. Anything that cannot move inside that time may not be relied on by the plan.

operator_priorities.statement: The detachment must be able to move within the hour, throughout.
Crypto and key management must never be interrupted.
The command post must remain available for the full mission.
Keep the shelter within equipment limits; a degraded setpoint is acceptable to buy endurance.
Keep the aid post powered if it does not threaten the signals task.
Minimise fuel: no resupply is assumed and every litre is carried.
Welfare and personal charging are discretionary.

notes: MM-DEMO-002 is an invented scenario written to test whether the MissionSpec generalises beyond MM-DEMO-001 (RQ-001). It does not reflect any armed forces requirement, doctrine, or real deployment.
It differs from MM-DEMO-001 in shape, not only in numbers: 48 hours rather than 72, no host-nation supply at any point, and mobility as a hard requirement rather than a note.

GEN-HV-01 is on site and is the most efficient source available. It is trailer-mounted, so a detachment that must displace within the hour cannot rely on it. Whether the planner respects that is the point of the mission.
Priority 1 is ADVISORY because the demonstrator does not model displacement as an event; it models what may be relied on if one is ordered.
No adversary behaviour is modelled. Disruption is represented only as asset unavailability.
